items.stem: A leader announces a change once in a town hall and expects adoption. Why is this likely to fail?

options.text: Change requires sustained communication, sponsorship and enablement, not a single announcement
options.rationale: Correct: adoption is built over time, not declared once.
They can help; the problem is relying on one event.

options.text: People always resist any change equally
options.rationale: Resistance varies and can be managed.
An announcement is not behaviour change.

items.explanation: Correct: sustained communication, sponsorship and enablement drive adoption.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO signs suggest low change readiness? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Past change initiatives stalled and were not followed through
options.rationale: Correct: a poor track record lowers readiness.

options.text: Key stakeholders are silent and disengaged
options.rationale: Correct: silence often masks resistance, not agreement.

options.text: Sponsors actively and visibly back the change
Teams ask informed questions about the plan
options.rationale: Engaged questions are a positive sign.

items.explanation: Correct: a history of stalled change and disengaged stakeholders both signal low readiness.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: After go-live, what best indicates the change has actually succeeded?

options.text: Sustained new behaviour and adoption metrics over time
options.rationale: Correct: success is sustained behaviour, not the go-live date.
On-time delivery is not the same as adoption.
Sending a message is not behaviour change.

options.text: The old system was switched off
options.rationale: Switching off the old system does not prove adoption.

items.explanation: Correct: sustained behaviour and adoption metrics, not go-live, indicate success.
